newsitem.title: USA: Florida legislature drafts $42.2 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: Florida legislature drafts $42.2 billion budget.

text.p: Florida lawmakers have reached agreement on a $42.2 billion budget proposal that increases public school funding by $610 million but fails to address a school construction backlog.

The budget was sent to the printer late Monday night. It was to be distributed to legislators Tuesday in order to meet a state-mandated 72-hour review period before a final vote ahead of the legislature's adjournment Friday.

Lawmakers were still trying to reach agreement on proposals to help fund $3 billion of needed public school construction. But any such agreement now would force the legislature to return in a special session.
The fiscal 1998 budget increases overall spending by 5.5 percent over this year, with no new taxes. Most of the new revenue results from economic growth and college tuition hikes.
The budget allocates $11 billion for public schools, an increase of $610 million over this year.

Tuition at public colleges and universities will rise by $30 million, or 7.8 percent for undergraduates, 12.8 percent for graduate students and out-of-state students, and 8.7 percent for community college students.
The budget increases health and human services spending by $207.4 million over this year, ending a recent trend of cutting those services to devote more money to education.
It raises criminal justice spending by $81.3 million, with most of the increase earmarked for prison construction.
The budget also includes $25 million to provide temporary aid to legal immigrants who will lose federal benefits as a result of welfare reform.

Lawmakers rejected Gov. Lawton Chiles' proposal to raise the state's cigarette tax to fund children's program, but approved a one-year cut of 0.5 percent in the unemployment tax that companies pay. They also raised the maximum weekly unemployment benefit by $25 to $275.

The legislature killed a $60 million sales tax rebate that National Football League Miami Dolphins owner Wayne Huizenga had sought for upgrades at Pro Player Stadium, formerly called Joe Robbie Stadium.
Huizenga already received a $60 million sales tax rebate for his Florida Marlins National League baseball team, which plays at the same stadium.
